instructions: Durable scheduling for this worker. schedule_list exposes authorized targets and saved schedules. schedule_create saves one-time or repeating future work. schedule_get, schedule_update, schedule_run_now, schedule_history and schedule_retire manage those schedules. This native MCP capability is separate from connected-service capability brokers. The saved worker or receiving application handles the instruction and configured output for each occurrence; the calling worker manages the schedule. A confirmed save or start normally needs one short, natural confirmation of the useful timing and destination. Explain more when the user asks or a real decision needs it. Do not recite internal acceptance or delivery-validation rules, narrate why you did not duplicate the task, or claim a task result before it exists.

tools.schedule_create: Manage scheduling: save one-time reminders, timers, or repeating future work using an authorized supplied target. Read schedule_list for target choices; never invent a destination or request reference. A saved definition confirms the schedule, not completion of its future instruction.
tools.schedule_list: Manage scheduling: list available reminder/timer targets and existing schedules within this worker's current grants. Use a returned target unchanged when creating a schedule.
tools.schedule_get: Manage scheduling: read a reminder, timer, or repeating work definition within the current supplied target grants.
tools.schedule_update: Manage scheduling: edit, pause, or resume a reminder, timer, or repeating work definition within the current supplied target grants.
tools.schedule_retire: Manage scheduling: stop future occurrences of a reminder, timer, or repeating work definition within the current supplied target grants. This does not retract already accepted work.
tools.schedule_run_now: Manage scheduling: start one saved reminder, timer or repeating work occurrence. Its saved worker or receiving application does the work and handles the configured output. You manage the schedule: do not execute the saved instruction yourself or poll after a successful start. Use a unique key for each new request; reuse it only for retries. occurrence_created means new (true), recovered (false), or unknown (absent). Recovering an old occurrence does not start new work. For a distinct new request that reused an old key, use a fresh key. Never change keys for an uncertain retry. Explicit monitor/wait requests and separately requested work still apply.
tools.schedule_history: Manage scheduling: read reminder/timer occurrence and delivery history when checking requested status or diagnosing a failed run. A successful schedule_run_now already starts the saved executor; no history check or polling is needed to make that work run or deliver. Accepted delivery does not mean application work completed.
